analyst_view.overall: Early view: a low-scoring pairing of two sides on 12 points. Eder Sarabia's Espanyol keep the ball (64% against Deportivo) but have only 13 goals and lack Kike García until December, while Bordalás's Getafe have 8, the fewest in the league, and play in Tbilisi in the Conference League four days earlier. Gudelj serves his yellow-card ban against Atlético on 22 November, so he should be available here.

goals.text: The numbers say 1.9 goals. Espanyol have scored twice in their last three games and Getafe have 8 goals all season, with one shot on target at Villarreal. I agree with a low total; under 2.5 looks right.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.5 corners. Espanyol's last three games had 14, 10 and 13 corners, and at home under Sarabia they keep the ball against deep blocks (9 corners against Deportivo); Getafe defend deep away and gave up 9 at Villarreal. I lean slightly higher, around 10-11.

cards.text: The numbers say 7 cards, which is high but fits: Espanyol had four yellows against Deportivo and five at Racing, and Getafe's games against Rayo and Sevilla each had a red card. Gudelj should be back, and Terrats and Riedel are one yellow from bans. I stay with the number.

shots.text: The numbers say 23.6 shots. Espanyol's possession has not turned into volume (11 shots against Deportivo, 5 at Villarreal) and Getafe managed 9 at Villarreal. A slow Monday game after Getafe's trip to Georgia, with Bordalás already worried about fatigue, points lower, around 21.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 7.4 on target. Getafe put 1 of 9 on target at Villarreal and Espanyol's best chances against Deportivo were headers, with no proper striker while Kike García is out. I lean lower, around 6.
